header: The colour converter, RGB <-> HEX <-> HSL, laid out like the converter's other panels: RGB on the left (three boxes, red, green, blue, each 0 to 255), HEX in the middle (a dark panel), HSL on the right (three boxes, hue 0 to 360, saturation and lightness 0 to 100), and under them the colour itself with its three written forms. Type in any of the three and the other two follow; while what is typed is not a colour the other panels keep the last good one and say what is wrong. I keep HSL in whole numbers, so a colour typed in HSL comes back as the nearest RGB (the note under the panels says so). The sums are in colour.ts.

doc: One number box with a spinner: a small up arrow above the number and a down arrow below it, shown while the pointer is over the box (or the box is being typed in), so I keep them from covering the digits. The Up and Down keys do the same (Shift moves by 10). The arrows only write new text into the box, and I decide what that text means by the same reading as if it had been typed. I let an arrow that is pressed and kept pressed go on stepping, rapidly and one step at a time, until it is let go (holdRepeat.ts).

behaviours: the converter has a Colour (RGB · HEX · HSL) kind, last but one (before currency), with no units of its own and rgb/hex as its pair
opened on a colour, the card shows the colour panel and the kind in its dropdown, not the two unit boxes
it opens on #FF5733: red 255, green 87, blue 51 in the three RGB boxes and #FF5733 in the HEX box
the colour itself is shown under them, with both written forms, #FF5733 and rgb(255, 87, 51), on the colour (the ink is white or black by brightness)
it opens on #FF5733 as hsl(11, 100%, 60%): hue 11, saturation 100, lightness 60 in the three HSL boxes, and all three written forms under the colour
the three panels are RGB, HEX and HSL in that order, each can be copied, nothing is shown as wrong at first, and the note says HSL is in whole numbers
a colour typed as HSL reaches the card: 'hsl(0, 100%, 50%)' opens on #FF0000 with hue 0, and 'hsl(11, 100%, 60%) to rgb' is answered by the colour card
a three-digit start (#f53) opens as #FF5533 and an invalid start falls back to the default colour
the card's other kinds are unchanged: length still opens the two unit boxes
each of the six boxes (red, green, blue, hue, saturation, lightness) has a spinner: an Increase and a Decrease arrow, which are hidden until the pointer is over the box or it is being typed in
the arrows cannot be pressed while hidden (no stray taps), are buttons that are skipped by Tab, and the HEX box has none
'#ff5733 to rgb', 'rgb(255, 87, 51) to hex', '255,87,51 to hex' and 'rgb to hex' are answered as you type by the colour card
the answer carries the colour as a six-digit HEX: #ff5733 -> #FF5733, rgb(255,87,51) -> #FF5733, rgb to hex -> the default #4F46E5
other lines are not taken for a colour: a number, a unit conversion, a currency, a sum, a word of three hex letters
a unit converter question still opens the unit converter's form, not the colour
